note.explanation: This chapter connects work with energy and power. It covers how forces transfer energy, how kinetic and potential energy are calculated, and how efficiently machines convert energy.
examples: A 20 N force pulls a box 3 m at 60° to its direction of motion: W = Fd cos θ = 20 × 3 × cos 60° = 30 J.
A 100 kg load raised 80 m in 25 s: P = mgh/t = 100 × 10 × 80 ÷ 25 = 3200 W.
note.checkAnswer: If the force is perpendicular to the displacement, the work done is zero because cos 90° = 0.
note.simple: Work is energy transferred when a force moves something. Kinetic energy is energy of motion, and potential energy is stored because of position. Power tells how quickly work is done.
note.checkQuestion: A 10 N force moves an object 2 m in the same direction as the force. How much work is done?
note.title: Work, Energy and Power
steps: Identify the force, displacement, angle, mass, speed, height, or time given in the question.
Choose the matching relation: W = Fd cos θ, KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, or P = W/t.
Substitute the values with their units and calculate carefully.
State the answer with its correct SI unit and check that it agrees with the question.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.1. Work done is maximum when the angle between the force F and the displacement d is:
(a) 0° (b) 30° (c) 60° (d) 90°
rationales: Correct: cos 0° = 1, so W = Fd is maximum.
Incorrect: cos 30° is less than 1, so the work is less than at 0°.
Incorrect: cos 60° is less than 1, so the work is less than at 0°.
Incorrect: cos 90° = 0, so the work is zero.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.2. A joule can also be written as:
(a) kg m s⁻² (b) kg m s⁻¹ (c) kg m² s⁻³ (d) kg m² s⁻²
rationales: Incorrect: kg m s⁻² is the unit of force, the newton.
Incorrect: kg m s⁻¹ is the unit of momentum.
Incorrect: kg m² s⁻³ is the unit of power, the watt.
Correct: 1 J = 1 N m = 1 kg m² s⁻².

mcqs.stem:
Q5.3. The SI unit of power is:
(a) joule (b) newton (c) watt (d) second
rationales: Incorrect: the joule is the SI unit of work and energy.
Incorrect: the newton is the SI unit of force.
Correct: power is measured in watts.
Incorrect: the second is the SI unit of time.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.4. The power of a water pump is 2 kW. The amount of water it can raise in one minute to a height of 5 metres is:
(a) 1000 litres (b) 1200 litres
(c) 2000 litres (d) 2400 litres
rationales: Incorrect: this amount would require less energy than the pump supplies in one minute.
Incorrect: this amount would require less energy than the pump supplies in one minute.
Incorrect: raising this amount through 5 m requires less than the supplied 120 000 J.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.5. A bullet of mass 0.05 kg has a speed of 300 m s⁻¹. Its kinetic energy will be:
(a) 2250 J (b) 4500 J (c) 1500 J (d) 1125 J
rationales: Correct: KE = ½ × 0.05 × 300² = 2250 J.
Incorrect: this is twice the value from the kinetic-energy formula.
Incorrect: this does not result from substituting the given mass and speed into KE = ½mv².
Incorrect: this is half the correct kinetic energy.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.6. If a car doubles its speed, its kinetic energy will be:
(a) the same (b) doubled
(c) increased to three times (d) increased to four times
rationales: Incorrect: kinetic energy depends on the square of speed.
Incorrect: doubling speed does not merely double kinetic energy.
Incorrect: the square of 2 is 4, not 3.
Correct: KE ∝ v², so doubling speed makes kinetic energy four times as large.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.7. The energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position is:
(a) kinetic energy (b) potential energy
(c) chemical energy (d) solar energy
rationales: Incorrect: kinetic energy is the energy a body has because of its motion.
Correct: potential energy is associated with a body's position.
Incorrect: chemical energy is stored in chemical substances.
Incorrect: solar energy comes from the Sun.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.8. The magnitude of momentum of an object is doubled, the kinetic energy of the object will:
(a) double (b) increase to four times
(c) reduce to one-half (d) remain the same
rationales: Incorrect: for the same mass, kinetic energy depends on the square of momentum.
Correct: KE = p²/(2m), so doubling p makes KE four times as large.
Incorrect: doubling momentum increases rather than reduces kinetic energy.
Incorrect: the kinetic energy changes when the momentum changes.

mcqs.stem:
Q5.9. Which of the following is not renewable energy source?
(a) Hydroelectric energy (b) Fossil fuels
(c) Wind energy (d) Solar energy
rationales: Incorrect: hydroelectric energy is renewable when water is continually replenished.
Correct: fossil fuels are finite and take millions of years to form.
Incorrect: wind is naturally replenished.
Incorrect: sunlight is naturally replenished.

written.text: Q5.1. A force of 20 N acting at an angle of 60° to the horizontal is used to pull a box through a distance of 3 m across a floor. How much work is done?

rubric.why: The work relation must account for the angle between force and displacement.
rubric.description: Select the work formula for an angled force.

rubric.why: Correct substitution shows how the given values are used.
rubric.how: Use F = 20 N, d = 3 m and θ = 60°.

rubric.why: The final value and unit are needed for full credit.
rubric.description: Calculate and state the final work.
rubric.how: Evaluate the expression and state joules.

written.text: Q5.2. A body moves a distance of 5 metres in a straight line under the action of a force of 8 newtons. If the work done is 20 joules, find the angle which the force makes with the direction of motion of the body.

rubric.why: The angle must be found using the work relation for a force at an angle.
rubric.description: Write the work relation and substitute values.

rubric.why: Rearranging correctly isolates the cosine of the angle.
The angle is the requested final result.
rubric.how: Use the angle whose cosine is 0.5.

written.text: Q5.3. An engine raises 100 kg of water through a height of 80 m in 25 s. What is the power of the engine?

rubric.why: Power is work done per unit time, and the work here is the gain in gravitational potential energy.
Substituting the mass, height, time, and gravitational field strength gives the needed calculation.
rubric.how: Use g = 10 m s⁻² and the given values.

rubric.why: The final answer must be the correct power with its SI unit.

written.text: Q5.4. A body of mass 20 kg is at rest. A 40 N force acts on it for 5 seconds. What is the kinetic energy of the body at the end of this time?

rubric.why: The acceleration is needed to find the body's final speed.
The final speed follows from the acceleration and the time.
The correct kinetic energy and unit complete the solution.
rubric.how: Use KE = ½mv² and give the answer in joules.

written.text: Q5.5. A ball of mass 160 g is thrown vertically upward. The ball reaches a height of 20 m. Find the potential energy gained by the ball at this height.

rubric.why: The mass must be converted to kilograms for the SI calculation.
Gravitational potential energy depends on mass, gravitational field strength, and height.
rubric.description: Use and substitute into the potential-energy relation.
rubric.how: Write PE = mgh and use g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The correct gained energy and unit are required.

written.text: Q5.6. A 0.14 kg ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 35 m s⁻¹. Find the maximum height reached by the ball.

rubric.why: At maximum height the initial kinetic energy has changed into gravitational potential energy.
The equation must be rearranged and the given speed and g substituted.
rubric.description: Find h from the energy relation.
rubric.how: Cancel mass and rearrange to h = v²/(2g).

rubric.why: The height, including its unit, is the requested result.

written.text: Q5.7. A girl is swinging on a swing. At the lowest point of her swing, she is 1.2 m from the ground, and at the highest point she is 2.0 m from the ground. What is her maximum velocity and where?
written.finalAnswer: 4 m s⁻¹, at the lowest position

rubric.why: The vertical height difference gives the change in potential energy.
rubric.how: Subtract the lowest height from the highest height.

rubric.why: The lost potential energy becomes kinetic energy as the girl swings down.
rubric.description: Relate the energy change to speed.
rubric.how: Set mgh equal to ½mv² and rearrange.

rubric.why: The answer needs both the maximum speed and its position.
rubric.description: State the maximum speed and where it occurs.
rubric.how: Use g = 10 m s⁻² and identify the lowest point as the point of maximum speed.

modelAnswer: Loss in potential energy = gain in kinetic energy
v = √(2 × 10 × 0.8) = 4 m s⁻¹, at the lowest position

written.text: Q5.8. A person pushes a lawn mower with a force of 50 N making an angle of 45° with the horizontal. If the mower is moved through a distance of 20 m, how much work is done?

rubric.why: The work formula accounts for the angle between force and horizontal displacement.
Correct substitution uses the force, displacement, and angle.
rubric.how: Use F = 50 N, d = 20 m, and θ = 45°.

rubric.why: The final work must be stated in joules and agree with the printed answer.

written.text:
Q5.9. Calculate the work done in

(i) Pushing a 5 kg box up a frictionless inclined plane 10 m long that makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal.

rubric.why: The vertical height is required to find the gain in gravitational potential energy.
On a frictionless incline, the work equals the increase in potential energy.
rubric.how: Use W = mgh with g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: The correct work and unit are the required final result.

written.text:
Q5.9. Calculate the work done in

(ii) Lifting the box vertically up from the ground to the top of the inclined plane.

rubric.why: The top of the incline is 5 m above the ground.
rubric.description: Find the vertical height of the top.
rubric.how: Use the incline length and angle to obtain h = 10 sin 30°.

rubric.why: The work lifting the box equals its increase in gravitational potential energy.
The final work with the correct unit earns the final marks.
rubric.how: Substitute m = 5 kg, g = 10 m s⁻², and h = 5 m.

written.text: Q5.10. A box of mass 10 kg is pushed up along a ramp 15 m long with a force of 80 N. If the box rises up a height of 5 m, what is the efficiency of the system?

rubric.why: Efficiency uses the useful energy output of lifting the box.
rubric.how: Find mgh using the vertical height.

rubric.why: The input work is the applied force multiplied by the distance along the ramp.
Efficiency is the useful output divided by input, expressed as a percentage.

written.text: Q5.11. A force of 600 N acts on a box to push it 5 m in 15 s. Calculate the power.

rubric.why: The work done is needed before power can be calculated.
Power is work divided by time.
The final power with its SI unit is required.
rubric.how: Give the calculated result in watts.

written.text: Q5.12. A 40 kg boy runs up-stair 10 m high in 8 s. What power he developed.

rubric.why: The boy's gain in potential energy is the work done against gravity.
Power depends on the work done and the time taken.
The final power and unit are necessary for full credit.

written.text: Q5.13. A force F acts through a distance L on a body. The force is then increased to 2F that further acts through 2L. Sketch a force-displacement graph and calculate the total work done.

rubric.why: Work is represented by the area under a force-displacement graph.
rubric.description: Identify how work is represented on the graph.
rubric.how: State that work is the area under the graph.

rubric.why: The first part has force F acting through distance L.
rubric.description: Find work in the first section.

rubric.why: The second part has force 2F acting through a further distance 2L.
rubric.description: Find work in the second section.

rubric.why: The total work is the sum of both sections and must match the stated result.

modelAnswer: Work is the area under the force-displacement graph.
For the first distance L: W₁ = F × L = FL

examTips: The exercise tests definitions and explanations in short-answer and constructed-response questions, and calculation methods in numerical problems.
For an angled force, show W = Fd cos θ, substitute the values, and give the answer in joules.
For kinetic energy, show KE = ½mv²; for gravitational potential energy, show PE = mgh. Convert mass to kilograms before substituting.
Power questions usually require P = W/t. For a raised load, first use W = mgh.
For efficiency, show both useful output work and input work, then use efficiency = (useful output/input) × 100%. Include the percentage sign.
Marks are commonly earned for the correct formula, substitution, calculation, and final answer with units. Do not omit working even when the final answer is correct.

Substitute F = 20 N, d = 3 m and cos 60° = 0.5.

Substitute the mass, height, time, and g = 10 m s⁻² from the textbook method.
Calculate the work first, then divide by the time.

explain.title: Work
explain.body: Work is done when a force causes displacement. For a force making angle θ with the displacement, W = Fd cos θ. Work is measured in joules.

explain.title: Kinetic energy
explain.body: Kinetic energy is the energy of a moving body. Use KE = ½mv²; because speed is squared, doubling the speed makes kinetic energy four times as large.

explain.title: Potential energy
explain.body: A body raised above a reference level gains gravitational potential energy: PE = mgh. Height is measured vertically.

explain.title: Power and efficiency
explain.body: Power is the rate of doing work: P = W/t. Efficiency compares useful output work or energy with input work or energy, expressed as a percentage.

explain.title: Energy sources and conservation
explain.body: Energy changes from one form to another; it is not lost overall. Renewable sources are naturally replenished, while non-renewable sources are finite.

mistakes: Using W = Fd without including cos θ when force and displacement are not in the same direction.
Forgetting to square the speed in KE = ½mv².
Using the distance along a ramp instead of the vertical height in PE = mgh.
Leaving mass in grams instead of converting it to kilograms.
Writing power in joules instead of watts, or omitting units.
Reversing the efficiency fraction: use useful output divided by input, then multiply by 100%.
